purpose: State/transition correspondence contract between executable evaluator and PG-009 formal recovery model.

mappings.note: Python admissibility is assurance-level scoped; this mapping is a release safety condition, not full semantic equivalence.

concurrency_scenarios.expected: second acquisition is blocked while a current recovery owner exists
stale owner cannot act because transition requires owner identity and current recovery authority epoch
a second release is blocked because release authorization is consumed and state leaves QUARANTINED/CLOSED
a second immediate commit is blocked because the first commit leaves ADMITTED and enters RUNNING
authority epoch changes and admitted execution is blocked until fresh admission
RUNNING or ADMITTED execution is interrupted to OFFLINE and the gate closes

notes: Concurrency is modeled as atomic state transitions; this is not yet a proof of implementation-level CAS/linearizability.
Recovery owner identity is now an explicit transition input for revalidation and release authorization; recoveryAuthorityEpoch fences stale authority.
Double-release and double-commit are transition-precondition properties, not universal at-most-once effect guarantees.

Authority revocation is modeled as a hard admission fence: ADMITTED/RUNNING transitions to OFFLINE with stop/gate enforced, requiring fresh recovery before execution can resume. This does not claim physical cancellation of an already-completed external effect.
